summary: Olympic NF summit: a 1943 AWS cabin, then a 1956 R-6 tower removed or destroyed in 1971. No source describes remains today.

facts.design: R-6 flat-top cab on a 40-ft treated timber tower (1956); earlier AWS cabin
facts.status_note: Tower removed or destroyed in 1971; no source describes a standing structure.

staffing.status: used as a summer fire lookout (state memo, 1943); no named lookouts found

access.note: Walk on Olympic National Forest land. None of the pages read mentions a gate or closure.

visit.trail_note: 1.3 miles one way, about 700 ft of gain, along an old road off FR 2923. The author says the road is brushy, with fallen trees.

facts.remains_note: Photo captions on WillhiteWeb name post footings, an outhouse foundation, a battery, a fry pan and phone line wire; one caption is dated 2020. No standing structure is described.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS dates the cabin to 1943; WillhiteWeb dates the AWS station to 1942; the Weebly listing has 1943. The story gives both dates and says they differ.
FFLOS gives 15x18 ft; the 1944 AWS report quoted by WillhiteWeb gives 12x16 ft. The story reports both.

FFLOS, firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb give 40 ft for the 1956 tower; a 1956 newspaper item quoted by WillhiteWeb says 30 ft. The record's 12.2 m (40 ft) is kept, with the disagreement noted in the story.
All four sources agree on 1971. The register says removed; the other three say destroyed. The story reports both words.

sources.title: Hyas Mountain Lookout Site
sources.publisher: Former Fire Lookout Sites (National Register of Former Lookout Sites)

notes_for_editor: Dates and dimensions conflict across sources and the story says so: 1943 and 15x18 ft (FFLOS) vs 1942 and 12x16 ft (WillhiteWeb, quoting an AWS report). The 1956 tower is 40 ft in three sources and 30 ft in one 1956 newspaper item quoted on two pages; the record's 12.2 m was kept. The Weebly copy of the newspaper item has a typo ('Hias'), so the WillhiteWeb wording was used. No lookout names were found for Hyas in the pages read. One WebSearch surfaced no new Hyas sources. No photos recorded. Correction on review: an earlier draft said no source described what is left on the summit. WillhiteWeb's photo captions name post footings, an outhouse foundation and debris. The firelookout.com header reads 'R.I.P. 1943-1956' while its body and three other sources give 1971, so the story keeps 1971.
